To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TIMP- 1 is a tumor inhibitor in the BALB/C CT26 mouse model of metastasis.
TIMP- 1 has a tumor inhibitory role in the CT26 mouse model of liver metastasis and this is independent of the cell type and method used to modulate TIMP-1 expression.
the over-expression of TIMPs in tumor cells leads to tumor growth inhibition, whereas their knockdown has the opposite effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the paradoxical tumor promoting and tumor inhibiting effects of TIMP- 1.
the role of the proteolytic network in tumor growth and metastasis.
the role of tissue inhibitors of metalloprotienases (TIMPs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the BALBC/CT26 model TIMP-1 acts tumor inhibitory and that the tumor promoting effects of TIMP- 1 observed in other tumor models might be attributed to the specific tumor type, the target cell or the mode of gene transfer.
TIMP- 1 is tumor inhibitory in the liver metastasis model of the BALB/c mouse and that the observed paradoxical results in other systems are due to the use of different animal models.
TIMP- 1 is tumor inhibitory in the BALB/CT26 model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the CT26 model, TIMP- 1 is a tumor inhibitor and TIMP-2 is a tumor promoter, while the effects of TIMP-3 are not as clear cut.
TIMP-2 is a tumor promoting factor, and that TIMPs-1 and TIMPs-3 are tumor inhibitory factors in the CT26 mouse model of metastatic colorectal cancer.
TIMP- 1 has a strong tumor inhibitory effect, but that this effect can be masked by other TIMP-1 effects, e.g. in the context of inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of TIMP- 1 modulation on cancer development and metastases depends on the type of target tissue and the model used.

TIMP- 1 is an important player in tumor growth and progression in the liver and that it is not only a potential target for therapeutic intervention, but also an important biomarker for the prediction of the clinical outcome of liver metastases.
in vivo studies are needed to determine the role of TIMPs in cancer development and progression.
